idiom_name: QObject view-model with Q_PROPERTY(... NOTIFY ...) exposed to QML binding expressions
implementation_notes: Qt is the canonical C++ home: the view-model is a QObject whose Q_PROPERTY declares READ/WRITE and, crucially, a NOTIFY signal - without NOTIFY a property cannot participate in QML property bindings - while Qt 6's QBindable/QObjectBindableProperty add bindable properties for computed values. The view is a .qml document that binds to those properties declaratively and invokes slots or Q_INVOKABLE methods as commands, and QML's dependency engine re-evaluates only the bindings that read a changed property. Emit NOTIFY only when the value actually changed; the Qt docs warn that unnecessary emissions force needless binding re-evaluation.
pitfalls: Without a NOTIFY signal on a Q_PROPERTY, QML bindings to it never update - a silent, property-by-property failure.
A property changed directly through its MEMBER does not emit NOTIFY, so bindings go stale; use the setter (or Q_OBJECT_BINDABLE_PROPERTY) instead.
Two-way bindings recurse when the setter does not guard equal values: bindings write back on every emission.
QObject thread affinity: view-models exposed to QML must live on the GUI thread; emitting from worker threads corrupts bindings.

variants.name: GTK/GObject property bindings (gtkmm or the C API)
variants.implementation_notes: Outside Qt, GTK's GObject layer is the other C++ binding runtime: a GObject-derived view-model exposes notifying properties, g_object_bind_property connects two properties (G_BINDING_BIDIRECTIONAL for editors) and GtkExpression plus .ui <binding> elements bind widget properties to expression-valued state. Choose it when gtkmm/GTK is already the toolkit; Qt Quick remains the default because its binding language and tooling are richer.
pitfalls: Property changes must call g_object_notify_by_pspec; GObject only auto-notifies for sets made through g_object_set().
Bindings hold references: unbind (g_binding_unbind) when widgets or view-models are destroyed, and keep all GTK calls on the main thread.
